# RFQ Response Comparison Tool — Single-Page Prototype Plan

## 1) Prototype overview
This single-page prototype demonstrates how procurement teams can compare multiple supplier quotes side-by-side and quickly arrive at a recommendation. Users land on the home page and either drag-and-drop files into an upload area or click “Use sample quotes” to instantly load three realistic mock quotes. Sliders let users adjust weights for Price, Delivery time, Payment Terms, and Compliance; the comparison matrix updates instantly. Each supplier column displays cost breakdowns, total cost of ownership (TCO), compliance badges, and a compact visual chart. A recommendation banner highlights the top supplier based on weighted scoring with a short rationale (e.g., “Best TCO, passes all compliance, on-time delivery”). This shows the core UX: fast normalization, automated scoring, and transparent evaluation without backend or persistence.

This single-page prototype demonstrates the core UX of validating a Shopify product CSV before import. # Prototype overview

This single-page prototype demonstrates a visual workflow for building regex-based redirect patterns and immediately testing them against sample URLs. Users assemble a pattern from predefined segments (e.g., literal, slug, number, wildcard, optional) using a point-and-click palette, name capture groups, and toggle anchors. A live regex preview updates in real time with a copy-to-clipboard action. Users paste multiple sample URLs into a tester that validates matches and displays captured groups. The page also generates redirect rule examples for Apache, Nginx, Cloudflare, and Next.js in tabbed code blocks, and shows a plain-English explanation of what the pattern matches along with edge-case warnings. # Prototype overview

This single-page prototype at src/app/page.tsx demonstrates how a user can “scan” a documentation site for WCAG compliance and quickly understand risks and fixes. The user pastes or selects a sample URL, clicks Run scan, and sees a simulated scan progress that resolves to a compliance score, AA/AAA indicators, and a prioritized issue list grouped by severity and category (e.g., alt text, contrast, headings). Users can filter issues by severity and category, expand an issue to see plain-language remediation guidance, effort estimates, and a mock legal risk score. A Download report action produces a mock JSON file and a toast confirming the “download.” The page uses mock data only, but the interactions and information architecture reflect the core UX of the product: assess, prioritize, and remediate. # Prototype overview

This single-page prototype demonstrates a Stripe Webhook Event Logger & Debugger UI that streams mock webhook events, lets users filter and search them, and inspect a selected event’s payload and a simple diff versus its previous related event. The page includes an environment toggle (Test/Live), pre-built filter pills for common scenarios (failed payments, subscription changes, disputes), and a search input that filters across event types and payload text. The main content shows a real-time event list with status badges and retry counts; selecting an event opens a details panel with metadata, JSON payload (copyable), and a “Replay” button that simulates a replay action via toast notification. The layout is responsive and accessible, with keyboard focus states, ARIA labels, and color contrast that works in both light and dark modes. This single-page prototype demonstrates a three-step flow for small businesses to create barcodes from a spreadsheet and preview printable labels while simulating basic scanning and activity tracking. Users will upload a CSV (or load sample data) to preview an inventory table, then configure a prefix and sequential numbering to generate Code 128 barcodes for each item. webhook testing & inspector:
Prototype overview
This single-page prototype demonstrates a webhook debugging flow by letting users generate a unique webhook URL, view a live-updating list of captured requests, inspect details, and simulate responses—all in the browser with mock data. At the top, the user sees their generated webhook URL with copy/regenerate actions and a “Send test webhook” button to simulate incoming requests. The left column lists recent webhook requests with method badges, paths, timestamps, and status indicators, plus a search/filter bar. Selecting a request reveals detailed tabs (Summary, Headers, Body, Query, Raw) with syntax-highlighted JSON. A Response Simulator lets users choose a status code and delay to visualize how a webhook endpoint would respond. A Replay Bar allows entering a target URL and “replaying” a captured webhook (shows toasts only). The layout is responsive, keyboard-accessible, and styled with Tailwind, reflecting design principles like hierarchy, contrast, and clear affordances.
